species.look_here_first: Start with the seedhead and nodes. King Ranch bluestem has smooth/glabrous nodes and a loose terminal head of only about 3–8 long fingerlike branches. The stems often kink/change angle at nodes and branch freely from a broad crown. That is very different from silver bluestem's dense cottony mass and cane bluestem's hairy nodes.

species.look_here_first: Look at the basal leaves first: huge, stiff, deeply pinnatifid blades cut almost to the midrib into narrow lobes. Then check the towering flowering stem and yellow ray-and-disk heads. Leaf north-south orientation is variable and not diagnostic by itself.

species.look_here_first: Start with the lower leaves: in local var. texanum, broad serrate blades narrow into winged petioles, while tiny narrow leaves occur high on the flowering branches. Distal stems are densely hairy and widely spreading branches have densely short-bracted flower stalks. FNA var. texanum involucres typically 3.8–5.2 mm, heads bluish-white; compare glabrous stalks and 27–36 rays in S. eulae.
